# Introduction for the project

Aging is relevant to the functional decline of normal HSCs as well as increased risk of hematologic malignancies in human. Abnormal clonal hematopoiesis which frequently occurs in the HSCs of the elderly is caused by DNA mutation in specific loci and shortening telomerase. Besides, there are several emerging intrinsic factors such as increased polarity, reactive oxygen species, and injured autophagy and mitochondria metabolism as ample evidence of aging of HSCs, which show the main features of aged HSCs compared to that of young HSCs (PMID: 31887851).

Our previous experiment

The aim of this study is to compare old and young HSC with low and high mitochondria membrane potential. Is there a difference in the chromatin and is this the difference in old and young populations?

# Sequencing data

There is 12 samples in the dataset: - 3x old low MMP - 3x old high MMP - 3x young low MMP - 3x young high MMP

Data was sequenced by the genomics facilty at WEHI on 20240619 (folder quinnS_151223) by the NextSeq2000 in one run (1.2 billion reads) 66 bp reads.

# Processing data with diffHic pipeline

To create the SLURM scripts for alignment for each sample:

```{r}

targets<-read.csv("/stornext/General/data/academic/lab_allan/Hannah/20230605_HSC_HiC_ageing_project/Fastq/20240603_Experimental_information_quinnS_Hi-C_YandO_MMP_hi_low_HSC.csv",
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#Remove the .gz part
targets$Read1<-substr(targets$Read1,1,nchar(targets$Read1)-3)
targets$Read2<-substr(targets$Read2,1,nchar(targets$Read2)-3)

# Set location of output
location<-"/vast/projects/coughlan.h.project/20230606_Old_young/20240603_MMP_Hi_Low_HSCs/Processing/"

#Location of fastq files
fastq.loc<-"/vast/scratch/users/coughlan.h/Fastq/20240603_MMP_Hi_Low_HSCs/stephen_w_QS/"

#Output tmp files
tmp.loc<-"/vast/scratch/users/coughlan.h/tmp/"

#strings
ALIGN<-"_aligned"
BAM<-".bam"
SORT<-"_sort"
FMI<-"_FMI"
MD<-"_MD"

#file names
samples<-paste0(targets$Sample,"_",targets$Rep)
output<-paste0(tmp.loc,"Aligned/",samples)
    
#Make SLURM script per sample
for (i in 1:length(samples)){
                    
                    fastqc_1_command<-paste0("fastqc ",fastq.loc,targets$Read1[i],".gz")
                    fastqc_2_command<-paste0("fastqc ",fastq.loc,targets$Read2[i],".gz")
                    
                    unzip1_command<-paste0("unpigz -p 32 ",fastq.loc,targets$Read1[i],".gz")
                    unzip2_command<-paste0("unpigz -p 32 ",fastq.loc,targets$Read2[i],".gz")
                    
                    align_command<-paste0("~/Python_install/python_3_8_8_test/bin/python3 ~/20210719_Scripts/presplit_map_t32.py -G /vast/projects/coughlan.h.project/bowtie2_mm39/mm39 -1 ",
                                          fastq.loc,targets$Read1[i]," -2 ",
                                          fastq.loc,targets$Read2[i]," --sig GATCGATC --cmd bowtie2 -o ",output[i],ALIGN,BAM)
                    
                    zip1_command<-paste0("pigz -p 32 ",fastq.loc,targets$Read1[i])
                    zip2_command<-paste0("pigz -p 32 ",fastq.loc,targets$Read2[i])
                    
                    FMI_command <- paste0("FixMateInformation I=",output[i],ALIGN,BAM, 
                                  " O=",output[i],ALIGN,FMI,BAM, " MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM=1000000 VALIDATION_STRINGENCY=SILENT AS=false SO=coordinate TMP_DIR=",tmp.loc,"tmp_FMI_",samples[i])
            
                    MD_command <- paste0("MarkDuplicates I=",output[i],ALIGN,FMI,BAM, " O=",output[i],ALIGN,FMI,MD,BAM, 
                                 " M=",output[i],"_mark_dup_metrices.txt VALIDATION_STRINGENCY=SILENT MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM=1000000 REMOVE_DUPLICATES=false tmp_DIR=",tmp.loc,"MD_com_",samples[i])
            
                    SORT_command <- paste0("samtools sort --threads 32 -n -O bam -o ",output[i],ALIGN,FMI,MD,SORT,BAM, " -T ",tmp.loc,"tmp_SORT_",samples[i]," ",output[i],ALIGN,FMI,MD,BAM)
                    
                    script.file<-paste0("#!/bin/bash","\n",
                                        "#SBATCH --job-name=",samples[i],"_HiC","\n",
                                        "#SBATCH --time=48:00:00","\n",
                                        "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=32","\n",
                                        "#SBATCH --mem=64G","\n",
                                        "#SBATCH --output=SLURM_stout_",samples[i],"\n",
                                        "#SBATCH --error=SLURM_err_",samples[i],"\n",
                                        "\n",
                                        "module purge","\n",
                                        "module load python","\n",
                                        "module load bowtie2","\n",
                                        "module load cutadapt","\n",
                                        "module load fastqc","\n",
                                        "module load pigz","\n",
                                        "module load biobambam2","\n",
                                        "module load samtools","\n",
                                        "module load picard-tools","\n",
                                        "export TMPDIR=/vast/scratch/users/coughlan.h/tmp","\n",
                                        "\n",
                                        #fastqc_1_command,"\n",
                                        #fastqc_2_command,"\n",
                                        unzip1_command,"\n",
                                        unzip2_command,"\n",
                                        align_command,"\n",
                                        zip1_command,"\n",
                                        zip2_command,"\n",
                                        FMI_command,"\n",
                                        MD_command,"\n",
                                        SORT_command)
                    write.table(script.file,paste0(tmp.loc,"20240620_SLURM_align_",
                                                   samples[i]),row.names=F,col.names=F,quote = FALSE)
                    
                }
                
                #Make overall script to launch jobs
                write.table(paste0("sbatch ",tmp.loc,"20240620_SLURM_align_",samples), 
                            file=paste0(tmp.loc,"20240620_SLURM_all_align_samples.sh"),
                            row.names=F,col.names=F,quote = FALSE)
```

# Mapping reads to restriction fragments

As HiC is based on ligation between restriction fragments the reads are actually two different restriction fragments containing the interaction loci. Therefore we report the reads in terms of the restriction fragment in the genome to which that read was mapped. We now create the fragment library for the genome required to create anchors for the data with the mm39 genome (the same one the samples were mapped to) and MboI restriction size.

We can now map the paired-end reads in the bam file to restriction fragments in the reference genome. The fragments to which the reads are mapped are now referred to as anchors. Each read of the paired-end read is aligned separately to a restriction fragment therefore each paired-end read records two different restriction fragment locations.

Only the 5′ end(s) will be used to determine the restriction fragment index for that read pair. The total number of chimeric read pairs will be reported, along with the number where 5′ ends or 3′ ends are mapped. Of course, the function will also work if the mapping location is only given for the 5′ end, though chimeric statistics will not be properly computed. The proportion of invalid chimeric pairs can then be calculated.

Invalid pairs are those where the 3′ location of a chimeric read disagrees with the 5′ location of the mate. The invalid proportion can be used as an empirical measure of the mapping error rate - or, at least, the upper bound thereof, given that error rates are likely to be lower for longer, non-chimeric alignments. High error rates may be indicative of a fault in the mapping pipeline.

Duplicate reads have previously been marked and will also be reported.

Open the fragments of the genome and set up the processed bam file location.

```{r}
library(diffHic)
library(edgeR)
mm39.frag<-cutGenome("~/Reference_genomes/mm39/mm39.fa", "GATC",4)
mm.param<-pairParam(mm39.frag)
mm.param
```

## Artifact removal

In this process of read mapping discover that some reads are most likely artefacts and not true chimeric reads originating from two different locations in the genome. Read pairs mapping to the same restriction fragment provide little information on interactions between fragments. Dangling ends are inward-facing read pairs that are mapped to the same fragment. These are uninformative as they are usually formed from sequencing of the restriction fragment prior to ligation. Self-circles are outward-facing read pairs that are formed when two ends of the same restriction fragment ligate to one another. Interactions within a fragment cannot be easily distinguished from these self-circularization events. Both structures are removed to avoid confusion in downstream steps.

To determine whether a read is a dangling end or self-circling read we can plot the strand orientation of the two ends as a function of insert size. The strand orientation for a read pair refers to the combination of strands for the two alignments. If different pieces of DNA were randomly ligated together, one would expect to observe equal proportions of all strand orientations. This can be tested by examining the distribution of strand orientations for read pairs. At high insert sizes, the distributions will converge for all strand orientations. At lower insert sizes, spikes are observed in the outward- and inward-facing distributions due to self-circularization and dangling ends, respectively. We set thresholds after the spikes to remove artefacts.

The length of the sequencing fragment is inferred by summing the distance between the mapping location of the 5′ end of each read and the nearest restriction site on the 3′ end of that read. The threshold value can be chosen based on the size selection interval in library preparation, or by examining the distribution of inferred fragment length.

```{r}
for (i in samples[11]){     
            diags <- getPairData(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,"_mm.h5"), mm.param)
            #create a histogram of the fragments
            pdf(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_combined_hist.pdf'))
            hist(diags$length[diags$length < 1500], ylab="Frequency", xlab="Spacing (bp)", main= paste0(i,'histogram fragment length'))
            abline(v=800, col="red", lty=2) 
            dev.off()
            
            png(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_combined_hist.png'))
            hist(diags$length[diags$length < 1500], ylab="Frequency", xlab="Spacing (bp)", main= paste0(i,'histogram fragment length'))
            abline(v=800, col="red", lty=2) 
            dev.off()
            
            #Create a plot of fragment orientations
            min.inward<- 1000
            min.outward<- 1000
            llinsert <- log2(diags$insert + 1L) 
            intra <- !is.na(llinsert) 
            breaks <- seq(min(llinsert[intra]), max(llinsert[intra]), length.out=30) 
            inward <- hist(llinsert[diags$orientation==1L], plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            outward <- hist(llinsert[diags$orientation==2L] ,plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            samestr <- hist(llinsert[diags$orientation==0L | diags$orientation==3L], plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            samestr$counts <- samestr$counts/2
            ymax <- max(inward$counts, outward$counts, samestr$counts)/1e6 
            xmax <- max(inward$mids, outward$mids, samestr$mids) 
            xmin <- min(inward$mids, outward$mids, samestr$mids)
            pdf(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_combined_insertsizes.pdf'))
            plot(0,0,type="n", xlim=c(xmin, xmax), ylim=c(0, ymax),xlab=expression(log[2]~"[insert size (bp)]"), ylab="Frequency (millions)", 
                 main= paste0(i,' insert size')) 
            lines(inward$mids, inward$counts/1e6, col="darkgreen", lwd=2) 
            abline(v=log2(min.inward), col="darkgrey") 
            lines(outward$mids, outward$counts/1e6, col="red", lwd=2) 
            abline(v=log2(min.outward), col="darkgrey", lty=2) 
            lines(samestr$mids, samestr$counts/1e6, col="blue", lwd=2) 
            legend("topright", c("inward", "outward", "same"), col=c("darkgreen", "red", "blue"), lwd=2)
            dev.off()
            
            png(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_combined_insertsizes.png'))
            plot(0,0,type="n", xlim=c(xmin, xmax), ylim=c(0, ymax),xlab=expression(log[2]~"[insert size (bp)]"), ylab="Frequency (millions)",
                  main= paste0(i,' insert size')) 
            lines(inward$mids, inward$counts/1e6, col="darkgreen", lwd=2) 
            abline(v=log2(min.inward), col="darkgrey") 
            lines(outward$mids, outward$counts/1e6, col="red", lwd=2) 
            abline(v=log2(min.outward), col="darkgrey", lty=2) 
            lines(samestr$mids, samestr$counts/1e6, col="blue", lwd=2) 
            legend("topright", c("inward", "outward", "same"), col=c("darkgreen", "red", "blue"), lwd=2)
            dev.off()
}
```

Distribution of interaction frequency information:

```{r}
cis_trans<-list()
disb_frq<-list()

for (i in samples){    
            diags <- getPairData(file=paste0(location,"Processed/",i,"_mm.h5"), param=mm.param)
            
            #Cis/trans numbers
            cis_trans[[i]]<-table(is.na(diags$insert))
            
            intra<-diags$insert[!is.na(diags$insert)]
            
            breaks <- c(0,100,200,300,400,500,1000,2000,5000,10000,25e3,50e3,75e3,100e3,150e3,200e3,300e3,500e3,1e6,2e6,5e6,10e6,20e6,50e6,100e6,150e6,200e6) 
            inward <- hist(intra, plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            png(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_barplot.png'))
            barplot(inward$counts/nrow(diags), names=inward$breaks[-1]/1e3, las=2,ylab="Proportion of interactions", 
                    xlab="Span bin (kbp)", main=paste0("Distribution of interaction frequency binned by span: ",i))
            
            dis<-inward$counts
            names(dis)<-inward$breaks[-1]
            disb_frq[[i]]<-dis
            dev.off()
                    
}       
saveRDS(cis_trans, "20240620_cis_trans.rds")
saveRDS(disb_frq, "20240620_disb_frq.rds")
```

## Mitochondrial reads

We investigate the number of trans mitochondria reads as a metric of data quality.

```{r}
mito_reads<-function(files){
    #####################################All chromosomes extracted###########################################
    library(rhdf5)
    all_sams<-list()
    for (n in files){
        #Get the names of all the chromosomes
        chroms.1<-h5ls(n)$name[h5ls(n)$otype=="H5I_GROUP"]
        number.1<-list()
        number<-list()
        
        for (k in chroms.1[!grepl("chrM",chroms.1)]){
             OW <- nrow(h5read(n, k)$chrM)
             if (is.null(OW)){
                 number.1[[k]] <- 0
             } else
                number.1[[k]] <- OW
        }
        
        #Open the hdf5 file with the chrom
        data.chr <- h5read(n, "chrM")
        for (k in chroms.1){
             if (is.null(nrow(data.chr[[k]]))){
                 number[[k]] <- number.1[[k]] + 0
             } else
                number[[k]] <- nrow(data.chr[[k]])
        }
        
        all_sams[[n]]<- (sum(unlist(number))-unlist(number)[("chrM")])/unlist(number)[("chrM")] }
        return(all_sams)
}
```

## Trimming artefacts

Now we remove the artifacts from the libraries by setting threshold of the inferred fragment lengths (max.frag) and minimum insert size based on strand orientation (min.outward/min.inward).

```{r}
min.inward<- 1000
min.outward<- 1000
max.frag<-800
for (i in samples){
            prunePairs(file.in=paste0(location,"Processed/",i,"_mm.h5"), mm.param, 
                       file.out = paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_mm_trim.h5'),
                       max.frag = max.frag,
                       min.inward = min.inward,
                       min.outward = min.outward)
}
```

Distribution of interaction frequency information:

```{r}
cis_trans<-list()
disb_frq<-list()

for (i in samples){    
            diags <- getPairData(file=paste0(location,"Processed/",i,"_mm_trim.h5"), param=mm.param)
            
            #Cis/trans numbers
            cis_trans[[i]]<-table(is.na(diags$insert))
            
            intra<-diags$insert[!is.na(diags$insert)]7
            
            breaks <- c(0,100,200,300,400,500,1000,2000,5000,10000,25e3,50e3,75e3,100e3,150e3,200e3,300e3,500e3,1e6,2e6,5e6,10e6,20e6,50e6,100e6,150e6,200e6) 
            inward <- hist(intra, plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            png(paste0(location,"Processed/",i,'_barplot_trim.png'))
            barplot(inward$counts/nrow(diags), names=inward$breaks[-1]/1e3, las=2,ylab="Proportion of interactions", 
                    xlab="Span bin (kbp)", main=paste0("Distribution of interaction frequency binned by span: ",i))
            
            dis<-inward$counts
            names(dis)<-inward$breaks[-1]
            disb_frq[[i]]<-dis
            dev.off()
                    
}       
saveRDS(cis_trans, "20240621_cis_trans_trim.rds")
saveRDS(disb_frq, "20240621_disb_frq_trim.rds")
```

# Decay curves

Note: move the hdf5 files to vast/projects:

```{r}
hdf5.location<-"/vast/projects/coughlan.h.project/20230606_Old_young/20240603_MMP_Hi_Low_HSCs/Processed/"
```

Decay curves (will plot the replicates together):

Define a function for getting the points:

```{r}
get_decay_curve <- function(file,param, break_size) {
                    diags <- getPairData(file=file, 
                                         param=param)
            
                    intra<-diags$insert[!is.na(diags$insert)]
                    breaks <- seq(0,300e6,break_size)
                    inward <- hist(intra, plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            
                    cum_sum<-as.data.frame(cbind(span=inward$breaks[-1],
                                                 freq=(inward$counts/break_size)/length(diags$insert)
                                                 )
                                           )
                    return(cum_sum)
}



get_decay_curve_per_chrom <- function(file,param, break_size) {
                    diags <- getPairData(file=file, 
                                         param=param)
            
                    intra<-diags$insert[!is.na(diags$insert)]
                    breaks <- seq(0,300e6,break_size)
                    inward <- hist(intra, plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            
                    cum_sum<-as.data.frame(cbind(span=inward$breaks[-1],
                                                 freq=(inward$counts/break_size)/length(diags$insert)
                                                 )
                                           )
                    return(cum_sum)
}

get_decay_curve_intra <- function(file,param, break_size) {
                    diags <- getPairData(file=file, 
                                         param=param)
            
                    intra <- diags$insert[!is.na(diags$insert)]
                    breaks <- seq(0,300e6,break_size)
                    inward <- hist(intra, plot=FALSE, breaks=breaks) 
            
                    cum_sum<-as.data.frame(cbind(span=inward$breaks[-1],
                                                 freq=(inward$counts/break_size)/length(intra)
                                                 )
                                           )
                    return(cum_sum)
}
```

Loop over the samples:

```{r}
decay_curves<-list()

for (i in samples){
    decay_curves[[i]]<-get_decay_curve(paste0(hdf5.location,i,"_mm_trim.h5"),
                                       break_size = 1e3, 
                                       param=mm.param)
}

saveRDS(decay_curves, "20240624_decay_curves.rds")
```

Open file and clean up the data frame:

```{r}
decay_curves<-readRDS("20240624_decay_curves.rds")
decay_curves<-do.call("cbind",decay_curves)

decay_curves<-as.data.frame(cbind(Span=decay_curves[,1], 
                                  decay_curves[,!grepl("span",colnames(decay_curves))]
                                 )
                            )

colnames(decay_curves)<-unlist(strsplit(colnames(decay_curves),split = ".freq"))
head(decay_curves)
```

## Zoomed out plots

Write a plotting function:

```{r}
plot_decay_curve <- function(samples_to, colours, xmin=4.0, xmax=8, ymin=-11, ymax=-5.0, name="Decay curves"){
                           
                            plot(log10(samples_to[,1]),
                                 log10(samples_to[,2]),
                                 xlim=c(xmin,xmax),
                                 ylim=c(ymin,ymax),
                            ylab="Average interaction frequency (log10)",
                            xlab="Interaction distance (log10) bp",
                            type = "l", col=colours[1],
                            main=name)
                            for (i in c(3:ncol(samples_to))){
                                points(x = log10(samples_to[,1]),
                                       y = log10(samples_to[,i]),
                                type = "l",
                                col = colours[c(i-1)])
                            }
                            legend("bottomleft", legend=colnames(samples_to)[-1],
                            col=(colours), lty=1, cex=0.7,lwd = 2)
}
```

Plot all samples:

```{r}
plot_decay_curve(samples_to = decay_curves, colours = col,
                 name="Decay curves: all samples")
```

```{r}
plot_decay_curve(samples_to = decay_curves[,c(1:7)], colours = col[c(1:6)],
                 name="Decay curves: all old samples")
```
